# grafts <a href="https://pkg.mitchelloharawild.com/grafts/"><img src="man/figures/logo.svg" align="right" height="139" alt="grafts website" /></a>

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/mitchelloharawild/grafts/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/mitchelloharawild/grafts/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

grafts (**gra**ph **f**orecasts for **t**ime **s**eries) is an interactive
browser app for exploring aggregated time series, such as hierarchical,
grouped and nested series, and their forecasts.

![The grafts explorer app](man/figures/app.png)

## Installation

You can install the development version of grafts from
[GitHub](https://github.com/mitchelloharawild/grafts) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("mitchelloharawild/grafts")
```

## Usage

grafts explores time series stored in a [tsibble](https://tsibble.tidyverts.org/)
whose keys have been aggregated with `aggregate_key()`. Any structure of keys
works, whether hierarchical (`State / Region`), grouped (`Purpose * State`) or a
mix of both.

```{r example, eval = FALSE}
library(grafts)
library(fable)

tourism_agg <- aggregate_key(
  tsibble::tourism, Purpose * (State / Region), Trips = sum(Trips)
)
grafts(tourism_agg)
```

`grafts()` makes an explorer, which opens in the viewer or a browser when
printed in the console. The data stays in R, which serves each series only when
it is drawn, so large collections of series open quickly. Like a Shiny app, the
console waits while the explorer is open: press Ctrl+C (or Esc in RStudio and
Positron) to stop it.

To also explore forecasts, pass a [fable](https://fable.tidyverts.org/) of
forecasts for those series to `forecasts`. Each model's forecasts and intervals
are drawn after the data.

```{r forecasts, eval = FALSE}
tourism_fc <- tourism_agg |>
  model(ets = ETS(Trips), snaive = SNAIVE(Trips)) |>
  forecast(h = "2 years")
grafts(tourism_agg, forecasts = tourism_fc)
```

## Exploring

The explorer starts from the total of all series. Its left side shows the
**series graph**, where each node is a series and its children sum to it.
Clicking a node lists the ways it can be split, such as by `Purpose` or
`State`, and choosing one adds those disaggregates to the graph. Below it, the
**dimension graph** shows the structure of keys and highlights where the
explorer is.

The right side plots the series being explored above its disaggregates, which
can be shown as small multiples, overlaid, stacked (to see what each
contributes to the total) or as seasonal plots. Clicking a time plot focuses
that series, and hovering a node highlights its series wherever it is plotted.
Right-clicking a node collapses its children, and shift-clicking pins it so
series from different parts of the graph can be compared side by side.

## Deploying

To serve the explorer from a server, add it to a plumber2 api with
`api_grafts()`, which takes an explorer from `grafts()` or the data and
arguments to make one. In a plumber2 file, such as for
Posit Connect:

```{r deploy-file, eval = FALSE}
#* @plumber
function(api) {
  api_grafts(api, readRDS("tourism_agg.rds"))
}
```

In Docker, listen on all interfaces:

```{r deploy-docker, eval = FALSE}
readRDS("tourism_agg.rds") |>
  grafts_serve(host = "0.0.0.0", port = 8000, launch = FALSE)
```

Several explorers can share one api by giving each a `path`, such as
`api_grafts(api, tourism_agg, path = "/tourism/")`.

## Embedding

Small collections of series can be explored without R, on a static web page
such as a pkgdown site, a blog or GitHub Pages. An explorer from `grafts()`
in an R Markdown or Quarto chunk, or in Shiny with `renderGrafts()`, is written
into the page with every series, and a page can hold several explorers.
`grafts_save()` writes one to a single HTML file.

```{r embed, eval = FALSE}
tourism <- grafts(tourism_agg, forecasts = tourism_fc, height = 600)
tourism  # in a chunk
grafts_save(tourism, "tourism.html")
```

`grafts_options()` chooses the views offered, the starting view and theme, and
whether visitors' choices persist, wherever the explorer goes.
Whether series add up to their parents is detected, hiding the Stacked view and
share scales for means.

```{r options, eval = FALSE}
grafts(tourism_agg, options = grafts_options(
  views = c("grid", "season"), theme = "dark", persist = FALSE
))
```

Every series is written into the page, so large collections are better served
from R, in the console or with `api_grafts()`. Embedded explorers use the system's UI font, unless the
page loads [Source Sans 3](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Source+Sans+3) as
the app does.
